```{=html}
<div role="note" class="study-note" aria-label="Using these lessons"><div class="note-mark" aria-hidden="true">i</div><div><h2>Connect algebra and geometry.</h2><p>Lesson 1 covers Chapter 1 of the Further Work with Vectors booklet: scalar-product properties, standard unit vectors, vector identities and the triangle inequality, through Examples 1.1–1.7. Lesson 2 covers Cauchy–Schwarz, triangle constructions and every geometric-proof example in Chapter 2 (Examples 2.1–2.17), in one deck that can be taught across two periods. Lesson 3 connects parametric coordinates to position vectors and develops vector, parametric and Cartesian equations of lines (Examples 3.1–3.7). Lesson 4 revisits Example 3.8, compares parallel and coincident lines, tests points on lines and establishes collinearity (Examples 3.9–3.13). Lesson 5 finds intersections in 2D and 3D, distinguishes skew lines, and connects minimum distance to the vector equation of a line (Examples 3.14–3.20). Lesson 6 connects parametric coordinates, position vectors and fixed-distance equations of circles, including starting points and direction of tracing (Examples 3.21–3.23). Lesson 7 develops sphere equations, intersections and the diameter interpretation of vector loci (Examples 3.24–3.31). Worked examples are completed in class. Follow the homework allocation at the end of each deck.</p></div></div>
```
